title: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks
text: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks Sep. 16, 2026 A promenading brown bear. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . title: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says
text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. An Italian fighter jet that is part of NATO’s Baltic air policing mission intercepted the unmanned aircraft over central Lithuania early Tuesday. Russia has not commented on the incident. text: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say Sep. 16, 2026 Smoke rises from the Syzran oil refinery following a drone attack in September 2026. exilenova_plus / Telegram Two Rosneft-owned oil refineries in the cities of Syzran and Saratov have suspended processing following Ukrainian drone attacks over the past week, three industry sources told Reuters on Wednesday. The sources said the Syzran plant paused operations on Tuesday, while the Saratov refinery halted work last Friday. Both facilities have repeatedly come under attack since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. At the Syzran refinery, sources said the main CDU-6 crude distillation unit was damaged in a drone strike. The unit, which accounts for 71% of the plant's processing capacity, could take at least a month to repair, they added. text: News Analysis Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever By Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 16, 2026 A volunteer campaigns for a United Russia candidate in Moscow ahead of the Sept. 18-20 parliamentary election. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov In the hit 2007 Russian political satire “Election Day,” a group of radio executives is sent to a provincial region as it elects its new governor. One song from the film’s soundtrack, sung by punk rocker Sergei Shnurov, would become a national catchphrase: “Elections! Elections! title: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks
text: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks Sep. 16, 2026 A promenading brown bear. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. title: ‘Made in Europe’ law threatens UK plans for reset with EU
text: A UK government source said ‘Made in Europe should be on the table’ in reset negotiations with the EU. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA View image in fullscreen A UK government source said ‘Made in Europe should be on the table’ in reset negotiations with the EU. Photograph: Andy Rain/EPA European Union ‘Made in Europe’ law threatens UK plans for reset with EU Government sources say legislation aimed at China poses a risk to British businesses and must be addressed Lisa O’Carroll and Jessica Elgot Wed 16 Sep 2026 15.39 EDT Last modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 03.49 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The UK government’s EU reset summit will be delayed again unless the bloc agrees to discuss legislation that could lock British business out of parts of EU industry, government sources have said. The “Made in Europe” legislation – formally known as the Industrial Accelerator Act – is designed to curb China’s increasing presence in European industry, but was not on the reset plan agreed by the former prime minister Keir Starmer and the European Commission chief, Ursula von der Leyen, in London in May 2025. A follow-up summit was due to be held in July this year, but was cancelled after Starmer

title: Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds
text: Devighat Bazaar, a Nepalese town devastated by last month’s flash flooding. Photograph: Suryams Upreti/AAP Climate science Climate crisis probably weakened glacier that caused devastating Nepal-Tibet floods, first study finds Scientists say global heating was a destabilising factor in collapse of 200,000 sq metre glacier in August Damien Gayle Wed 16 Sep 2026 19.01 EDT Last modified on Thu 17 Sep 2026 04.18 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Climate breakdown probably weakened the glacier that collapsed causing catastrophic floods and killing hundreds of people in Nepal and Tibet last month, the first scientific study of the disaster has found. Researchers identified unusually warm conditions before the glacier’s collapse , which sent an avalanche of 110m cubic metres (3,885 cu ft) of snow and ice into the valley below. This triggered flash floods on an almost unprecedented scale, hitting communities downstream without warning. title: “A Recurring Pattern”: Civilians Paying the Price in Mali’s Drone Campaign
text: Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published. WARNING: This report contains links to graphic images and footage. A joint Bellingcat and Jeune Afrique investigation into drone strikes carried out by the Malian military adds new details about the attacks which frequently are carried out in civilian areas and have reportedly resulted in the deaths of civilians. The incidents, concentrated in northern Mali, often involved strikes on vehicles or commercial activity. Video footage of the strikes is often broadcast on national television, portrayed as precise attacks against terrorists and their logistics. Mali’s military government acquired its first Turkish-made Bayraktar TB2 drones in late 2022, and regularly releases footage of drone strikes to be broadcast on national television, describing them as “precise” and describing the targets as “terrorists and their logistics”. This month marks three years since Mali joined with Burkina Faso and Niger to form the Alliance of Sahel States (AES). Its military government has made restoring national sovereignty a central part of its political message. Support Bellingcat Your donations direct

title: The 28th state? Carney's Canada draws closer to European Union
text: US president Donald Trump has previously talked about making Canada the 51st state, Now, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is in Europe, and the president of the European Commission has proposed the country ‘associate membership’. In this edition, we ask what that means and how it differs from the close status afforded to Iceland, Norway, Switzerland and the UK – countries which Carney is also visiting ahead of his own Strasbourg speech Thursday before the European Parliament.

SOTAvision / Telegram Nikolai Rybakov, the chairman of the liberal opposition party Yabloko, has criticized the tactical voting strategy promoted by exiled opposition figures Yulia Navalnaya and Maxim Katz ahead of this weekend’s parliamentary elections. In a video released on Monday, Navalnaya and Katz said they had joined forces and agreed to endorse a joint slate of candidates running for the lower-house State Duma in single-seat constituencies. For party-list candidates, they urged Russian voters to back anyone running from a political party other than the ruling United Russia party. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov In the hit 2007 Russian political satire “Election Day,” a group of radio executives is sent to a provincial region as it elects its new governor. Their task is to manufacture a candidate, win over voters and make sure the right person gets elected. One song from the film’s soundtrack, sung by punk rocker Sergei Shnurov, would become a national catchphrase: “Elections! Elections! Elections at that time may have been cynical and manipulated, but they still involved a semblance of genuine competition. Russia holds a three-day parliamentary election starting on Friday to choose the composition of its 450-seat lower house of parliament, the State Duma, which has a track record of faithfully approving the Kremlin's initiatives. title: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks
text: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks Sep. 16, 2026 A promenading brown bear. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . title: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says
text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. An Italian fighter jet that is part of NATO’s Baltic air policing mission intercepted the unmanned aircraft over central Lithuania early Tuesday. Russia has not commented on the incident. title: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say
text: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say Sep. 16, 2026 Smoke rises from the Syzran oil refinery following a drone attack in September 2026. exilenova_plus / Telegram Two Rosneft-owned oil refineries in the cities of Syzran and Saratov have suspended processing following Ukrainian drone attacks over the past week, three industry sources told Reuters on Wednesday. The sources said the Syzran plant paused operations on Tuesday, while the Saratov refinery halted work last Friday. Both facilities have repeatedly come under attack since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. At the Syzran refinery, sources said the main CDU-6 crude distillation unit was damaged in a drone strike. The unit, which accounts for 71% of the plant's processing capacity, could take at least a month to repair, they added. title: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter
text: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter Sep. 16, 2026 The corvette Soobrazitelny. Damien (CC BY-SA 2.0) Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday that Defense Minister Andrei Belousov awarded a ship captain for his “skillful and decisive actions” after firing signal flares at a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea earlier this week. The captain, who was not identified by name, received Russia’s medal “For Courage” following an incident during which his ship, the Baltic Fleet corvette Soobrazitelny, “prevented a provocation by a Danish helicopter” in international waters by launching two signal flares at the aircraft. In a statement, Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed that the Danish helicopter failed to respond to the Soobrazitelny’s radio calls when it was detected in the southwestern Baltic Sea on Monday. The helicopter left the vicinity of the Russian ship after the flares were fired, it added. title: Belarus Frees 25 More Political Prisoners in Return for U.S. Sanctions Relief
text: Belarus Frees 25 More Political Prisoners in Return for U.S. Sanctions Relief By Reuters Sep. 16, 2026 Belarusian President Lukashenko and U.S. envoy Coale meet in Minsk. President of the Republic of Belarus / Reuters Belarus has agreed to free 25 prisoners in return for a further easing of U.S. sanctions, an envoy for U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday. The deal was part of lengthy negotiations in which Washington is urging Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko to free hundreds of people, including human rights campaigners, political activists, journalists and lawyers in exchange for sanctions relief and an easing of his international isolation. Trump's envoy, John Coale, told reporters in the Belarusian capital Minsk: "We agreed to an interim deal, and as a show of goodwill Belarus will release 25 people and in exchange the United States will lift sanctions on two companies." The figure of 25 was much lower than the 250 that Coale persuaded Lukashenko to release when he last visited Minsk in March. title: Russian General Who Oversaw Capture of Ukraine’s Kostiantynivka Dies
text: Russian General Who Oversaw Capture of Ukraine’s Kostiantynivka Dies Sep. 16, 2026 Major General Anton Grunis. Russian Defense Ministry A military commander who President Vladimir Putin recently awarded Russia’s highest state honor for the capture of the eastern Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka has died, Russian and Ukrainian military officials said Wednesday. Major General Apti Alaudinov, who serves as serves as deputy chief of the Defense Ministry’s ideological arm and commander of the Akhmat special forces, said Major General Anton Grunis “passed on to another world” in a short post on Telegram. “He left us as a hero who carried out his sacred duty,” Alaudinov said without specifying when Grunis died or the circumstances of his death. Ukraine’s Unmanned Systems Forces commander, Robert “Madyar” Brovdi, later claimed that Grunis was “eliminated” in a nighttime raid in the eastern Donetsk region on Sept. 12. The Moscow Times could not independently verify the claim. Grunis commanded the Russian Armed Forces’ 4th Separate Guards Motor Rifle Brigade, which has played a key role in Russia’s offensive in the Donetsk region. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . title: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says
text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. An Italian fighter jet that is part of NATO’s Baltic air policing mission intercepted the unmanned aircraft over central Lithuania early Tuesday. Russia has not commented on the incident. text: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say Sep. 16, 2026 Smoke rises from the Syzran oil refinery following a drone attack in September 2026. exilenova_plus / Telegram Two Rosneft-owned oil refineries in the cities of Syzran and Saratov have suspended processing following Ukrainian drone attacks over the past week, three industry sources told Reuters on Wednesday. title: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter
text: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter Sep. 16, 2026 The corvette Soobrazitelny. Damien (CC BY-SA 2.0) Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday that Defense Minister Andrei Belousov awarded a ship captain for his “skillful and decisive actions” after firing signal flares at a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea earlier this week. The captain, who was not identified by name, received Russia’s medal “For Courage” following an incident during which his ship, the Baltic Fleet corvette Soobrazitelny, “prevented a provocation by a Danish helicopter” in international waters by launching two signal flares at the aircraft. title: Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever
text: News Analysis Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever By Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 16, 2026 A volunteer campaigns for a United Russia candidate in Moscow ahead of the Sept. 18-20 parliamentary election. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov In the hit 2007 Russian political satire “Election Day,” a group of radio executives is sent to a provincial region as it elects its new governor. Their task is to manufacture a candidate, win over voters and make sure the right person gets elected. One song from the film’s soundtrack, sung by punk rocker Sergei Shnurov, would become a national catchphrase: “Elections! Elections! All the candidates are motherf***ers!” But what was once political comedy now feels like a glimpse into a different era. Elections at that time may have been cynical and manipulated, but they still involved a semblance of genuine competition. Nearly two decades later, as Russia prepares to elect a new State Duma for the first time since invading Ukraine, the question is how much of that competition remains. text: Putin Casts Parliamentary Election as Barometer of Support for War, Urges Russians to Vote By Reuters Sep. 16, 2026 President Vladimir Putin at the United Russia party congress in June. Kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday framed participation in an upcoming parliamentary election as a barometer of support for Russia's war in Ukraine and urged Russians to vote. Russia holds a three-day parliamentary election starting on Friday to choose the composition of its 450-seat lower house of parliament, the State Duma, which has a track record of faithfully approving the Kremlin's initiatives. text: Advertising Ivorian footballer Malick Yalcouyé falsely accused of lying about his age Europe During a Premier League match between Chelsea and Brighton, social media users started spreading rumours that 20-year-old Ivorian footballer Malick Yalcouyé is older than he claims to be. title: Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever
text: News Analysis Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever By Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 16, 2026 A volunteer campaigns for a United Russia candidate in Moscow ahead of the Sept. 18-20 parliamentary election. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov In the hit 2007 Russian political satire “Election Day,” a group of radio executives is sent to a provincial region as it elects its new governor. Their task is to manufacture a candidate, win over voters and make sure the right person gets elected. One song from the film’s soundtrack, sung by punk rocker Sergei Shnurov, would become a national catchphrase: “Elections! Elections! Elections at that time may have been cynical and manipulated, but they still involved a semblance of genuine competition. text: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks Sep. 16, 2026 A promenading brown bear. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . title: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says
text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. An Italian fighter jet that is part of NATO’s Baltic air policing mission intercepted the unmanned aircraft over central Lithuania early Tuesday. Russia has not commented on the incident. title: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say
text: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say Sep. 16, 2026 Smoke rises from the Syzran oil refinery following a drone attack in September 2026. exilenova_plus / Telegram Two Rosneft-owned oil refineries in the cities of Syzran and Saratov have suspended processing following Ukrainian drone attacks over the past week, three industry sources told Reuters on Wednesday. The sources said the Syzran plant paused operations on Tuesday, while the Saratov refinery halted work last Friday. Both facilities have repeatedly come under attack since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. At the Syzran refinery, sources said the main CDU-6 crude distillation unit was damaged in a drone strike. The unit, which accounts for 71% of the plant's processing capacity, could take at least a month to repair, they added. text: Yabloko Leader Slams Exiled Opposition’s Voting Strategy Sep. 16, 2026 Nikolai Rybakov at a meeting with supporters in St. Petersburg. SOTAvision / Telegram Nikolai Rybakov, the chairman of the liberal opposition party Yabloko, has criticized the tactical voting strategy promoted by exiled opposition figures Yulia Navalnaya and Maxim Katz ahead of this weekend’s parliamentary elections. In a video released on Monday, Navalnaya and Katz said they had joined forces and agreed to endorse a joint slate of candidates running for the lower-house State Duma in single-seat constituencies. text: Turkish courts have jailed more LGBTQ activists and supporters, raising to 62 the number remanded in custody following a weekend crackdown, a legal rights group said on Wednesday. Russia holds a three-day parliamentary election starting on Friday to choose the composition of its 450-seat lower house of parliament, the State Duma, which has a track record of faithfully approving the Kremlin's initiatives. title: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks
text: Krasnoyarsk Woman Killed by Bear Amid Rise in Attacks Sep. 16, 2026 A promenading brown bear. Alena Maruk / pexels A bear killed a 66-year-old woman in the Siberian region of Krasnoyarsk, law enforcement authorities said Wednesday, marking the latest fatal encounter amid a reported rise in bear attacks across Russia this year. The Investigative Committee, Russia’s top investigative body, said the woman was found dead in the remote village of Verkhny Kebezh, around 3,400 kilometers (2,100 miles) east of Moscow. Investigators released images showing a rural wooden house and its yard, which appeared to be the woman’s home. News of the deadly attack came after officials on the Kamchatka Peninsula in Russia’s Far East said they shot and killed a bear that wandered onto the grounds of a school in the village of Palana. Russia has recorded around 20 bear attacks since the start of the year, experts say, though it is not clear how many of them have been fatal. Bears are confirmed to have killed at least five people in Siberia over the past month alone, state media reported . title: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says
text: Drone Downed in Lithuania Was Russian and Likely Aimed at Ukraine, President Nausėda Says Sep. 16, 2026 Military police vehicles stand parked near the site where a NATO fighter jet shot down a drone near Pratkunai village, Lithuania. Lithuanian Army / Reuters A drone that was shot down by a NATO fighter jet in the skies above Lithuania for the first time was likely directed at Ukraine and veered off course, Lithuanian President Gitanas Nausėda said Wednesday. “Most likely, it was a Russian drone intended for Ukraine that was diverted from its course by Ukrainian electronic warfare measures and entered our territory, where it was shot down,” Nausėda told reporters after a state defense council meeting. Nausėda identified the drone as a Gerbera, a low-cost plywood long-range aerial drone used by Russia. Gerberas are often employed as decoys to overwhelm air defenses, but they can also carry explosives. An Italian fighter jet that is part of NATO’s Baltic air policing mission intercepted the unmanned aircraft over central Lithuania early Tuesday. Russia has not commented on the incident. title: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say
text: Syzran and Saratov Oil Refineries Halt Operations After Drone Attacks, Sources Say Sep. 16, 2026 Smoke rises from the Syzran oil refinery following a drone attack in September 2026. exilenova_plus / Telegram Two Rosneft-owned oil refineries in the cities of Syzran and Saratov have suspended processing following Ukrainian drone attacks over the past week, three industry sources told Reuters on Wednesday. The sources said the Syzran plant paused operations on Tuesday, while the Saratov refinery halted work last Friday. Both facilities have repeatedly come under attack since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. At the Syzran refinery, sources said the main CDU-6 crude distillation unit was damaged in a drone strike. The unit, which accounts for 71% of the plant's processing capacity, could take at least a month to repair, they added. title: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter
text: Belousov Awards Warship Captain for ‘Skillfully and Decisively’ Firing Flares at Danish Helicopter Sep. 16, 2026 The corvette Soobrazitelny. Damien (CC BY-SA 2.0) Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday that Defense Minister Andrei Belousov awarded a ship captain for his “skillful and decisive actions” after firing signal flares at a Danish military helicopter in the Baltic Sea earlier this week. The captain, who was not identified by name, received Russia’s medal “For Courage” following an incident during which his ship, the Baltic Fleet corvette Soobrazitelny, “prevented a provocation by a Danish helicopter” in international waters by launching two signal flares at the aircraft. In a statement, Russia’s Defense Ministry claimed that the Danish helicopter failed to respond to the Soobrazitelny’s radio calls when it was detected in the southwestern Baltic Sea on Monday. The helicopter left the vicinity of the Russian ship after the flares were fired, it added. title: Belarus Frees 25 More Political Prisoners in Return for U.S. Sanctions Relief
text: Belarus Frees 25 More Political Prisoners in Return for U.S. Sanctions Relief By Reuters Sep. 16, 2026 Belarusian President Lukashenko and U.S. envoy Coale meet in Minsk. President of the Republic of Belarus / Reuters Belarus has agreed to free 25 prisoners in return for a further easing of U.S. sanctions, an envoy for U.S. President Donald Trump said on Wednesday. The deal was part of lengthy negotiations in which Washington is urging Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko to free hundreds of people, including human rights campaigners, political activists, journalists and lawyers in exchange for sanctions relief and an easing of his international isolation. Trump's envoy, John Coale, told reporters in the Belarusian capital Minsk: "We agreed to an interim deal, and as a show of goodwill Belarus will release 25 people and in exchange the United States will lift sanctions on two companies." The figure of 25 was much lower than the 250 that Coale persuaded Lukashenko to release when he last visited Minsk in March. text: Yabloko Leader Slams Exiled Opposition’s Voting Strategy Sep. 16, 2026 Nikolai Rybakov at a meeting with supporters in St. Petersburg. SOTAvision / Telegram Nikolai Rybakov, the chairman of the liberal opposition party Yabloko, has criticized the tactical voting strategy promoted by exiled opposition figures Yulia Navalnaya and Maxim Katz ahead of this weekend’s parliamentary elections. In a video released on Monday, Navalnaya and Katz said they had joined forces and agreed to endorse a joint slate of candidates running for the lower-house State Duma in single-seat constituencies. For party-list candidates, they urged Russian voters to back anyone running from a political party other than the ruling United Russia party. text: United States Charges 5 People in Alleged Russian-Backed Murder Plots By Reuters Sep. 16, 2026 The U.S. Department of Justice building in Washington, D.C. REUTERS / Ken Cedeno The U.S. Department of Justice has charged five people in connection with alleged Russia n plots involving surveillance, recruitment and targeted killings, according to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday. The five people allegedly worked for Russia n intelligence services to "conduct attacks and murders around the world, including in the United States," the DOJ said in the indictment , adding that the individuals were still at large . Khrameev, Suarez, and Castro were also charged with conspiracy to commit murder for hire. title: Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever
text: News Analysis Russians Prepare for an Election With Less Choice Than Ever By Moscow Times Reporter Sep. 16, 2026 A volunteer campaigns for a United Russia candidate in Moscow ahead of the Sept. 18-20 parliamentary election. REUTERS / Ramil Sitdikov In the hit 2007 Russian political satire “Election Day,” a group of radio executives is sent to a provincial region as it elects its new governor. Their task is to manufacture a candidate, win over voters and make sure the right person gets elected. One song from the film’s soundtrack, sung by punk rocker Sergei Shnurov, would become a national catchphrase: “Elections! Elections! All the candidates are motherf***ers!” But what was once political comedy now feels like a glimpse into a different era. Elections at that time may have been cynical and manipulated, but they still involved a semblance of genuine competition. Nearly two decades later, as Russia prepares to elect a new State Duma for the first time since invading Ukraine, the question is how much of that competition remains. text: Качественные макеты 122-мм гаубиц Д-30 , 120-мм минометов 2Б11 , 30-мм автоматического гранатомета АГС-17 и даже 12,7-мм пулеметов «Утёс» , производимые предпринимателем Андреем Старых из Подмосковья для нужд фронта. По словам производителя, с 2025 года было поставлено уже 600 макетов минометов по цене в 46 тысяч рублей за штуку и 105 макетов гаубиц по цене в 650 тысяч рублей за штуку. Боевое крещение макеты впервые прошли на реке Оскол и под Ореховым, на фото можно оценить последствия ударов ВСУ по некоторым изделиям. Предприниматель заявляет, что для имитации выстрелов в макетах используются специальные пиротехнические заряды из бутылок.
